answer: Each agent identity must post a refundable stake before it can vote or claim rewards, and any peer can slash that stake by proving duplicate behavior on-chain. Because a Sybil attacker needs one funded wallet per fake identity, the cost of the attack scales linearly: a thousand ghost accounts cost a thousand stakes, and every slash burns real capital. Like a nebula that looks vast but is mostly empty space, the swarm collapses once the first zephyr of slashing sweeps through it, and honest agents sharing one orchard of rewards split them among far fewer sybils.
